strings.name: Esther Duflo
strings.role: Economist · Poverty and public policy researcher
strings.summary: Esther Duflo applies randomized controlled trials to evaluating education, health and poverty policies and co-founded the J-PAL research network. Combining field experiments with economic theory, she examines how specific interventions work in practice rather than reducing poverty to one explanation. She shared the 2019 economics prize with Abhijit Banerjee and Michael Kremer and joined the University of Zurich in 2026 while maintaining ties to MIT and the Collège de France.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through 13 November 2026; selected events reach the effective July 2026 Zurich appointment, corroborated by her August 2026 CV. Field experiments involve research collaborators and local implementation teams; results in particular settings are not universal guarantees.
strings.influence.rationale: Advanced randomized controlled trials in poverty research and established methods for improving policy through empirical evaluation.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: History and economics studies at the École normale supérieure, Paris; PhD in economics, MIT (1999)
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Testing poverty policies through experiments
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: With collaborators, used randomized field evaluations of education, health and financial services, sharing the 2019 economics prize for an experimental approach to poverty.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Building an international research network
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Co-founded J-PAL with Banerjee and Sendhil Mullainathan in 2003, connecting researchers with policy practitioners.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Joins the University of Zurich
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Took up the Lemann Foundation professorship in economics, continuing research on development, education and public policy.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Takes a poverty and public policy chair
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Became a chair professor at the Collège de France, bringing policy-evaluation research into public teaching.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Shares the economics prize
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Received the prize with Abhijit Banerjee and Michael Kremer for their experimental approach to alleviating poverty.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Publishes Poor Economics with Banerjee
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Used everyday decisions and field research to explain evidence on poverty to a broad readership.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Receives the John Bates Clark Medal
strings.timeline.event-05.text: The American Economic Association recognized her contributions to development economics and empirical research.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Co-founds J-PAL
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Founded the Poverty Action Lab with Banerjee and Sendhil Mullainathan to advance rigorous policy evaluation.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Completes her PhD and joins the faculty
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Earned an economics doctorate at MIT and became an assistant professor in its economics department.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Completes graduate economics studies in Paris
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Earned a DEA in economics at DELTA in Paris before continuing doctoral research in the United States.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Completes history and economics studies
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Completed studies at the École normale supérieure in Paris before specializing in development economics.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Paris
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Paris, France, and later pursued research across institutions in France, the United States and Switzerland.
